newsitem.title: USA: U.S. appeals court upholds Kansas DNA testing law.
newsitem.headline: U.S. appeals court upholds Kansas DNA testing law.

text.p: A federal appeals court Monday upheld a Kansas law that requires some felons to submit to DNA testing so authorities can detect and deter repeat offenders.
The 10th Circuit Court of Appeals ruled 3-0 the law does not constitute an unreasonable search which the Constitution prohibits.

The law, passed by the Kansas legislature in 1991, requires convicted murderers and sex offenders to give blood and saliva samples that are sent for DNA testing. The results of the tests are kept for use in investigating future crimes.
The law was challenged by several prison inmates.
Similar laws in Virginia, Colorado and Oregon have been affirmed by various federal appeals courts.
